new_candidates.body:
## Description

Section 1a of [skills/isaac-sim-troubleshooting/SKILL.md](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim/blob/develop/skills/isaac-sim-troubleshooting/SKILL.md#section-1a-shutdown-hangs-kit-framework-deadlock) recommends a Python `SIGALRM` callback that calls `os.kill()` as a reliable watchdog for native teardown that holds the GIL indefinitely.

Kernel delivery of SIGALRM does not guarantee execution of the Python callback. In CPython, the low-level signal handler records a pending signal; the Python callback runs later in the main interpreter thread. A native call that never returns to the interpreter or checks pending signals can therefore prevent the callback from running indefinitely.

The [CPython documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/signal.html#execution-of-python-signal-handlers) explicitly documents this behavior. It is the same limitation that the skill already identifies for Python thread-based watchdogs.

There is also a smaller API typo: `os.alarm()` does not exist in Python's `os` module; the Unix API is `signal.alarm()`.

## Suggested documentation correction

- Remove the guarantee that a Python SIGALRM callback can escape a native GIL deadlock.
- Recommend an external process watchdog, or an appropriate native watchdog such as `faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(timeout, exit=True)` for a process that should terminate after a teardown deadline. Explain that force-exit bypasses cleanup.
- Point to the existing `SimulationApp._arm_shutdown_watchdog()` implementation and its `shutdown_watchdog_timeout` / `fast_shutdown` scope. That implementation already uses `faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(..., exit=True)`.
- Correct the `os.alarm()` reference.

References:

- [SimulationApp implementation](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim/blob/develop/source/extensions/isaacsim.simulation_app/isaacsim/simulation_app/simulation_app.py)
- [faulthandler.dump_traceback_later documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/faulthandler.html#faulthandler.dump_traceback_later)
- [Isaac Lab PR #7152](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/7152), which explains the same deferred-Python-signal limitation and uses a C-level faulthandler handler for hung-test diagnostics.

## Minimal reproduction

Tested on Linux with CPython 3.12.14. No Isaac Sim installation, GPU, or training workload is needed. `ctypes.PyDLL` retains the GIL around this native call. The native function stays in C after SIGALRM interrupts `pause()`, rather than returning to the interpreter.

Create `hold.c`:

```c
#include <unistd.h>

void hold_forever(void) {
    for (;;) {
        pause();
    }
}
```

Build it:

```bash
cc -shared -fPIC -O2 -o libhold.so hold.c
```

Create `child.py` next to the library:

```python
import ctypes
import faulthandler
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import sys

native = ctypes.PyDLL(str(Path(__file__).with_name("libhold.so").resolve()))
native.hold_forever.argtypes = []
native.hold_forever.restype = None

if sys.argv[1] == "python-signal":
    def callback(signum, frame):
        print("PYTHON_CALLBACK_RAN", flush=True)
        os._exit(23)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, callback)
    signal.alarm(1)
else:
    faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(1.0, exit=True)

print("ENTERING_NATIVE_CALL", flush=True)
native.hold_forever()
```

Run each case under an external deadline:

```bash
timeout -k 1s 3s python child.py python-signal
timeout -k 1s 3s python child.py native-watchdog
```

Observed in an equivalent `subprocess.Popen` parent harness with a three-second deadline:

| Mechanism | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Python SIGALRM callback, one-second alarm | Native call entered; callback sentinel never printed; parent had to kill the child after three seconds |
| faulthandler native watchdog, one-second deadline | Traceback emitted; child exited with status 1 after approximately one second, before the parent deadline |

This is a counterexample to the documentation's guarantee, rather than a reproduction of a particular Kit deadlock.

## Contribution scope

The [external contribution policy](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING_PATHS.md) currently excludes `skills/` from external PRs. Could a maintainer apply this focused documentation correction, or confirm the appropriate contribution route? No runtime behavior change is proposed.
new_candidates.title: Docs: Python SIGALRM callbacks cannot guarantee a GIL-independent shutdown watchdog
